title: Jose Mourinho made ‘huge mistake’ with Vinicius Jr comments, says Vincent Kompany
content:
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has said Jose Mourinho made a “huge mistake” in accusing Vinicius Junior of inciting an incident that ended with the Real Madrid forward alleging racist abuse.

Vinicius Jr alleged he had been racially abused by Benfica’s Argentine winger Gianluca Prestianni after scoring in the 50th minute of Tuesday’s Champions League tie between the two sides in Lisbon.

After the match, Mourinho, the Benfica head coach, said he had reminded Vinicius Jr, 25, that “the biggest person in the history of (Benfica)” — referring to their legendary forward Eusebio — “is Black” and said that “every stadium where Vinicius plays, something happens”.

Kompany used his press conference to offer support to the Brazil international, but he was also critical of Mourinho and accused the Portuguese of showing a lack of leadership.

“After the game, you have the leader of an organisation, Jose Mourinho, attacking the character of Vinicus Jr by bringing in his type of celebration to discredit what Vinicius is doing in this moment (highlighting the alleged racist comment),” Kompany said on Friday.

“For me, in terms of leadership, it’s a huge mistake and it’s something that we should not accept.”

Kompany continued: “On top of this, he mentions the name of Eusebio. To say that Benfica cannot be racist because the best player in the history of Benfica is Eusebio.

“Do you know what black players had to go through in the 1960s? Was he (Mourinho) there to travel with Eusebio to every away game? The only option (black players) probably had then was to be quiet and to say nothing and to be 10 times better and to get enough credit were people would say, ‘Actually, he’s good’.

“That was Eusebio’s life, probably, and today to use his name to make a point about Vinicius Jr who is finally in a situation where he can say something about it.”

And Kompany believes Vinicius Jr’s reaction to the incident “cannot be faked”.

“You can see it, it’s an emotional reaction, and I cannot see any benefit for him to go to the referee and taking all the misery on his shoulders,” the Bayern coach said. “There’s absolutely no reason for him to do this. I believe he did it more because he thought it was the right thing to do in that moment.”

Vinicius Jr’s Madrid team-mate Kylian Mbappe alleged that he had heard Prestianni “say that Vinicius is a monkey, five times”. Prestianni has denied the allegations.

“Kylian is usually really calm and really diplomatic with everyone, but he was really clear about what he heard and saw,” said Kompany.

“He was even clear when he talked about it after the game. So, all of this is happening, but then of course there’s a player who is hiding what he’s saying under his shirt. In the end, you have this side of it and unless that player comes forward it’s a difficult case.

“But then in the background you have people making monkey noises and there are signs it’s happening in the stadium as well. It’s happening. You can see it in the video. So, on the hand you have the altercation between the players, and on the other what’s happening in the stadium as well.”

The 39-year-old Belgian coach then returned to Mourinho, highlighting a series of the former Chelsea, Inter Milan, Real Madrid, Manchester United and Roma coach’s celebrations during his managerial career.

“When Jose Mourinho was doing that kneeslide at Old Trafford or when he went to the fans in semi-final for Inter Milan against Barcelona — when he did he celebration in front of the Barcelona fans — or when he played against Sevilla with Roma and was fighting with the referees and the referees had to go under protection and leave the country under protection after that game,” Kompany said.

“In that moment, if someone was racist to Mourinho, I would have hoped that all of us would have said ‘stop, his celebration doesn’t matter — let’s listen to what he has to say and let’s defend someone simple, core things.”
